text:
Damon Severson has 10 points in 21 games for Columbus and plays about 22 minutes a night. He scored against Toronto on November 21, set up Pyyhtia's shorthanded goal a few days later, and has four points in his last ten games, while the Blue Jackets won only three of those ten.

Some of the scoring won't last. His three goals came on 1.78 expected goals, our measure of chance quality, he is shooting 17.6% against a usual defenseman's 6.4%, and his teammates have scored about 11 more goals than expected with him on the ice. The underlying play is solid: Columbus has had 50.4% of the five-on-five expected goals with him out there, 3.31 points better than without him. Evolving-Hockey rated him 20th of 215 defensemen last season (2.4 wins above replacement), strong at both ends, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him at 6.1 primary shot assists per 60, 88th percentile. NHL EDGE clocks his top shot at 95.5 mph. Our numbers project 37 points.
headline: Severson's points are running ahead of the play
